verdict: Vertiv's sales surged 61% to $4.3B as data-center builders raced to add power and cooling, and net profit nearly doubled — the AI buildout is now the core of its business.

segments.name: Americas
segments.note: North and South America — power and cooling for data centers, up 75% YoY (66% organic).

segments.name: Asia Pacific
segments.note: Asia-Pacific data-center infrastructure — up 50% YoY (48% organic).

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Europe, the Middle East and Africa — up 23% YoY (19% organic), slower than the Americas but still fast.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and running a company growing this fast — up from $414M a year ago.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Non-cash amortization of technology and brands bought in past deals.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Other operating costs, including acquisition-related fair-value changes.

opex.name: Foreign currency loss
opex.note: Net losses from currency moves this quarter.

otherDetail: Other non-operating income of $17M, less net interest expense of $6M, for net other income of $11M.
oneTimers: Adjusted (non-GAAP) operating profit was $1,087M — a 25.2% margin — vs $984M GAAP; the gap is mostly the $65M of acquisition-intangible amortization. Adjusted EPS was $2.21 vs $1.95 GAAP.
footerNote: Vertiv reports to one decimal place; figures here are rounded to the nearest $1M, so net income is shown as $765M vs the reported $764.5M. Restructuring costs of $0.2M round to zero and are not a separate expense line. Segment sales are by region.

takeaways.title: The AI buildout, in one number
takeaways.text: Sales jumped 61% to $4.31B — 55% of it organic — and organic orders more than doubled. Every region grew at least 23%.

takeaways.title: Profit nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Net income rose 92% to about $765M and GAAP EPS to $1.95, as operating margin expanded on the surge in volume. Operating cash flow was $794M.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised again
takeaways.text: Vertiv lifted full-year 2026 sales guidance by $650M at the midpoint, to about $14.65B — management sees the data-center buildout accelerating, not pausing.
